skill_markdown:
# gigascience_indels_sav_non-reference_demonstration_sts26t-ge

## Overview

This Galaxy workflow is designed to generate a comprehensive non-reference protein database specifically tailored for neoantigen discovery using FragPipe. By integrating transcriptomic and genomic data, it identifies single nucleotide variants (SNVs), insertions/deletions (indels), and novel splice variants to create a customized FASTA database that extends beyond standard reference proteomes.

The pipeline begins by processing raw RNA-Seq reads, performing alignment with [HISAT2](https://toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/iuc/hisat2/hisat2/2.2.1+galaxy1) and transcript assembly via [StringTie](https://toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/iuc/stringtie/stringtie/2.2.3+galaxy0). Variant calling is executed using [FreeBayes](https://toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/devteam/freebayes/freebayes/1.3.6+galaxy0), while [CustomProDB](https://toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/galaxyp/custom_pro_db/custom_pro_db/1.22.0) is utilized to translate these genomic variations into potential protein sequences.

The final stages involve extensive data transformation and filtering to merge reference sequences (UniProt and cRAP) with identified variants. The workflow outputs several specialized FASTA files and SQLite databases, providing the necessary inputs for downstream proteogenomic analysis and Multi-Omics Visualization Platform (MVP) integration. This workflow is licensed under [CC-BY-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and is tagged for neoantigen research and Galaxy Training Network (GTN) applications.

## Inputs and data preparation

| Step | Label | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Homo_sapiens.GRCh38_canon.106.gtf | data_input | Human reference genome #!genome-build GRCh38.p13 #!genome-version GRCh38 #!genome-date 2013-12 #!genome-build-accession GCA_000001405.28 #!genebuild-last-updated 2021-11 |
| 1 | RNA-Seq_Reads_2.fastq | data_input | Second data set of RNA-seq data |
| 2 | RNA-Seq_Reads_1.fastq | data_input | First data set of RNA-seq data |
| 3 | HUMAN-Uniprot-and-isoforms_and_cRAP-FASTA-Database | data_input | HUMAN Uniprot+isoforms and cRAP FASTA database |


To prepare for this workflow, ensure you have the reference genome annotation in GTF format, paired-end RNA-Seq reads in FASTQ format, and a comprehensive protein database in FASTA format. While the workflow accepts individual datasets, organizing large-scale sequencing runs into paired dataset collections can significantly streamline the initial HISAT2 alignment and subsequent processing steps. It is essential to verify that your input FASTQ files are correctly assigned as R1 and R2 to maintain library integrity during mapping. For a comprehensive guide on parameter settings and specific database versions used in this demonstration, please refer to the README.md file. You can also automate the environment setup and job execution by using `planemo workflow_job_init` to generate a `job.yml` file.

## How to run (Planemo)

### Local Galaxy (default engine)

```bash
planemo run main-workflow.ga job.yml --download_outputs --output_directory . --output_json output.json
```

Optional: `--galaxy_root /path/to/galaxy` speeds up spinning up a local Galaxy.

### Docker Galaxy

Append e.g. `--engine docker_galaxy --ignore_dependency_problems` (requires Docker).

### External Galaxy (usegalaxy.org / EU / …)

```bash
planemo run main-workflow.ga job.yml --engine external_galaxy --galaxy_url SERVER_URL --galaxy_user_key YOUR_API_KEY
```

Create a reusable profile: `planemo profile_create myprofile --galaxy_url ... --galaxy_user_key ... --engine external_galaxy` then `planemo run main-workflow.ga job.yml --profile myprofile`.

### Job file

- Generate a template: `planemo workflow_job_init main-workflow.ga -o job.yml`
- Lint: `planemo workflow_lint main-workflow.ga`

See **[Running Galaxy workflows](https://planemo.readthedocs.io/en/master/running.html)** in the Planemo documentation.

## Invocation outputs

After a successful run with `--download_outputs`, files appear under your chosen `--output_directory`. `--output_json` records CWL-style metadata for outputs (paths, checksums).

On an external Galaxy, use `planemo invocation_download INVOCATION_ID --profile ...` to fetch outputs, or track progress with `planemo workflow_track INVOCATION_ID`.

Workflow steps marked as **workflow outputs** in the editor are listed under **Workflow outputs**; exact filenames depend on tools and Galaxy configuration.

## Files

- `main-workflow.ga` — Galaxy workflow export (JSON)
- `job.yml` — inputs/parameters for `planemo run` (create with `planemo workflow_job_init`)
- [Planemo: Running Galaxy workflows](https://planemo.readthedocs.io/en/master/running.html)
